stem:
Meena prepares a rose petal extract at home to test some substances.

The extract turns pink in lemon juice and green in soap solution.

She adds the extract to a sample of an unknown colourless liquid, and it turns pink.

What is the nature of the unknown liquid?

options.text: acidic, because it gives the same colour as lemon juice
basic, because it gives a different colour from soap solution
neutral, because the liquid itself is colourless
basic, because rose extract is a natural substance

teacher.key_rationale: The unknown liquid gives the same colour (pink) with rose extract as lemon juice, a known acid, so it is acidic. Option B is the trap for a student who reasons only from contrast with soap solution without matching the observed colour to the acidic reference.
